title: Narrow the Input Mismatch in Deep Graph Neural Network Distillation

problem.claim: Deep GNNs offer promising performance but their over-stacked structures incur high inference cost in deployment.

gap.claim: Existing graph-domain KD methods overlook the receptive-field, or input-information, gap between student and teacher GNNs, creating an input mismatch that complicates distillation.

contributions.claim: A lightweight stochastic extended module estimates missing input information for student GNNs.

The method models missing information with independent graph-level and conditional node-level distributions, optimizes both estimates using a Bayesian methodology, and combines them into a balanced estimate as additional student input.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors state that, to the best of their knowledge, this is the first work to address input mismatch in deep GNN distillation.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on extensive benchmarks reportedly show that the method outperforms existing KD methods for GNN distillation.
The authors report that the benchmark results confirm the estimations are reasonable and effective.

narrative_sequence.summary: Deep GNNs are promising because of over-parameterization and large receptive fields, but their depth increases deployment inference cost.
Knowledge distillation can compress deep GNNs into shallow students, but existing methods overlook the student-teacher input-information gap, termed input mismatch.
A stochastic extended module estimates missing information through graph-level independent and node-level conditional distributions, then supplies a balanced estimate as additional student input.
The authors identify the method as the first, to their knowledge, to address input mismatch in deep GNN distillation.
The authors report superior distillation performance against existing GNN KD methods on extensive benchmarks.
